hints: Write the expression in the completed square form $19 - (x-3)^2$.
Since $(x-3)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, deduce the maximum value of $f(x)$ and state the range.
walkthrough:
Determine the maximum value from the completed square form:
$$\text{Since } (x - 3)^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}, \text{ the maximum value is } 19$$

hints: Equate $g^{-1}(f(x)) = g(x)$, which simplifies to $f(x) = g(g(x)) = 16x + 5k$.
Rearrange into the quadratic equation $x^2 + 10x + (5k - 10) = 0$ and apply the single intersection condition $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ to solve for $k$.
Substitute $k$ back into the quadratic equation to find the single root $x$, then evaluate $y = g(x)$ to obtain the coordinates of $P$.
walkthrough:
Find the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$ for $g(x) = 4x + k$:
$$y = 4x + k \implies x = \frac{y - k}{4} \implies g^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - k}{4}$$

Set up the intersection equation $g^{-1}(f(x)) = g(x)$:
$$\frac{10 + 6x - x^2 - k}{4} = 4x + k \implies 10 + 6x - x^2 - k = 16x + 4k$$
$$x^2 + 10x + (5k - 10) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition (single meeting point $\implies b^2 - 4ac = 0$):
$$10^2 - 4(1)(5k - 10) = 0 \implies 100 - 20k + 40 = 0 \implies 20k = 140 \implies k = 7$$

Substitute $k = 7$ into the quadratic equation to find the $x$-coordinate of $P$:
$$x^2 + 10x + 25 = 0 \implies (x + 5)^2 = 0 \implies x = -5$$
